summary: Scope PG&E persisted MFA/session state and in-memory HTTP sessions to the named setup, serialize each setup's mutable authentication state with cancellation-aware acquisition, enforce the MFA delivery-selection transition, preserve account-discovery error classes, and honor REST request cancellation.
reason: Deep review found that multiple named PG&E/Opower setups shared a persisted state file and the global HTTP cookie jar; concurrent MFA, login, collection, account discovery, and interval reads could interleave mutable setup state; lock waits could outlive a canceled REST verification request; verification could silently choose Email before a delivery selection; account discovery replaced authentication and transport errors with an empty-account error; and REST verification detached upstream work from request cancellation.
validated_outcome: Two named PG&E setups use independent persisted state and HTTP cookie jars; all public and internal login, collection, account-discovery, interval, and MFA transitions serialize per setup with cancellation-aware lock acquisition; verification requires an explicit selected delivery method; cancellation reaches REST verification; and account-discovery authentication failures remain classified for callers.
